summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) — migrate the TEE worker into the monorepo apps/ structure with shared packages, add Phala Cloud CVM deployment, and verify end-to-end operation.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans completed across 4 waves. TEE worker restructured, 58 unit tests passing, CVM deployed to Phala Cloud production (not testnet), epoch key determinism and IPNS republish cycle verified. Security review performed and all high/medium findings fixed before shipping.

repo: Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier ($20 credit) runs on the same production nodes (Intel TDX hardware) as paid deployments. 'dstack-pha-prod5.phala.network' is the actual host.
TEE worker was moved from root tee-worker/ to apps/tee-worker/ as part of monorepo restructure. All cross-references, Dockerfile, and CI jobs updated accordingly.
Shared packages used by tee-worker: @cipherbox/crypto (ECIES), @cipherbox/core (IPNS signing), @cipherbox/sdk-core (KuboProvider, PsaProvider).
GitHub staging environment uses: PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY secret, STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET secret, PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL variable.
Docker host is at 192.168.133.12 (not .114 as previously recorded).

code.finding: Original code called getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking the private key into route scope. Fixed to use getPublicKey(). Also added epoch bounds validation (0-999) to prevent negative/huge epoch numbers.
Was reading TEE_EPOCH env var but the rest of the codebase uses TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH. Fixed to use consistent name.

Added MAX_BATCH_SIZE=100 limit to prevent unbounded ECIES decryption DoS. Removed dead keyEpoch field from interface. Eliminated redundant mutable successes/failures counters by deriving from results array.
req.path on 404 handlers creates unbounded Prometheus label cardinality. Fixed to use 'unmatched' fallback for unmatched routes.

TOCTOU DNS race: DNS lookup happened separately from HTTP fetch, enabling DNS rebinding attacks. Fixed by merging validateResolvedIp into ssrfSafeFetch with DNS pinning — resolve once, pin the IP for the actual connection. Headers API lowercases keys via entries(), so host header must be lowercase 'host' not 'Host'.
Route was reading TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH once at module load (stale after rotation). Fixed to read dynamically from request body. Added isValidCidFormat() CID validation for user-provided CIDs.
Key cache had no size limit — could grow unbounded with epoch enumeration attacks. Added MAX_CACHE_SIZE=100 with LRU eviction.

workflow: GSD pause-work/resume-work successfully transferred session state across machines (Mac dev box → Docker host). HANDOFF.json provides machine-readable state; .continue-here.md provides human-readable context.
When parallel Wave 2 agent spawning caused git config lock contention, sequential execution resolved it. Clean up stale worktrees before retrying.
classifyHandoffIfNeeded error from Claude Code is a runtime bug, not an agent failure — spot-check SUMMARY.md + commits to confirm real completion status.
Phala CLI deploy command: phala deploy -c docker-compose.phala.yml -n <name> -e 'KEY=value' --wait
Docker image for TEE worker pushed as ghcr.io/fsm1/cipherbox-tee-worker:v35-amd64 (not :latest) from Docker host.
Republish latency baselines: ~1155ms avg from remote machine to Phala Cloud prod5. Network-bound, not compute-bound. Co-located production deployment will be much faster.
Security review should happen before /simplify — code quality and security fixes can overlap and ordering matters.

friction: Wave 2 parallel agent spawn caused git config lock contention between agents — had to fall back to sequential execution.
Usage limit hit mid-Wave 2 execution (35-03 agent interrupted), requiring manual continuation.
gsd-tools init runs from wrong directory when in a worktree — had to explicitly cd to worktree path for init command.
Session transfer between machines required manual git pull on Docker host before /gsd:resume-work worked correctly.
HANDOFF.json was stale on the 'uncommitted Dockerfile' point after Docker host committed and pushed it — caused brief confusion.
Phase named 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' but Phala has no testnet — naming mismatch required documentation cleanup post-completion.
Headers API case sensitivity issue in SSRF tests: new Headers().entries() lowercases keys but direct Host header assignment was uppercase, causing 2 test failures after security fix.
